question: Show each order's id and date with the name of the customer who placed it.
expected_sql: SELECT o.id, o.ordered_on, c.name FROM handmade_shop.orders o JOIN handmade_shop.customer c ON c.id = o.customer_id

question: Which customers have never placed an order?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM handmade_shop.customer c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM handmade_shop.orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)

question: Which products have never been sold?
expected_sql: SELECT p.name FROM handmade_shop.product p LEFT JOIN handmade_shop.order_item i ON i.product_id = p.id WHERE i.order_id IS NULL

question: Which customers bought at least one product from the Kitchen category?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM handmade_shop.customer c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM handmade_shop.orders o JOIN handmade_shop.order_item i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN handmade_shop.product p ON p.id = i.product_id JOIN handmade_shop.category g ON g.id = p.category_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND g.name = 'Kitchen')

question: How many orders has each customer placed, counting customers with none as zero?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, count(o.id) AS order_count FROM handmade_shop.customer c LEFT JOIN handmade_shop.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name

question: Which customers have placed two or more orders?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM handmade_shop.customer c JOIN handmade_shop.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING count(*) >= 2

question: For each category, which two sold products brought in the most revenue?
expected_sql: SELECT category, product, revenue FROM (SELECT g.name AS category, p.name AS product, sum(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY g.id ORDER BY sum(p.price * i.quantity) DESC) AS position FROM handmade_shop.order_item i JOIN handmade_shop.product p ON p.id = i.product_id JOIN handmade_shop.category g ON g.id = p.category_id GROUP BY g.id, g.name, p.id, p.name) ranked WHERE position <= 2

question: What is the most expensive product and its price?
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM handmade_shop.product ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1

question: Which orders have a total value above the average order total?
expected_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT i.order_id, sum(p.price * i.quantity) AS total FROM handmade_shop.order_item i JOIN handmade_shop.product p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id) SELECT order_id, total FROM totals WHERE total > (SELECT avg(total) FROM totals)

question: List every employee with their manager's name, leaving it empty for anyone without a manager.
expected_sql: SELECT e.name, m.name AS manager FROM handmade_staff.employee e LEFT JOIN handmade_staff.employee m ON m.id = e.manager_id

question: Which employees earn more than their own manager?
expected_sql: SELECT e.name FROM handmade_staff.employee e JOIN handmade_staff.employee m ON m.id = e.manager_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary

question: Which employees earn more than the company-wide average salary?
expected_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM handmade_staff.employee WHERE salary > (SELECT avg(salary) FROM handmade_staff.employee)

question: Who is the highest-paid employee in each department?
expected_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, e.name FROM handmade_staff.employee e JOIN handmade_staff.department d ON d.id = e.department_id WHERE e.salary = (SELECT max(x.salary) FROM handmade_staff.employee x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id)

question: In each department, who earns one of the three highest distinct salaries?
expected_sql: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT d.name AS department, e.name, e.salary, dense_rank() OVER (PARTITION BY d.id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM handmade_staff.employee e JOIN handmade_staff.department d ON d.id = e.department_id) ranked WHERE salary_rank <= 3

question: Which departments pay an average salary above 6000?
expected_sql: SELECT d.name, round(avg(e.salary), 2) AS average_salary FROM handmade_staff.department d JOIN handmade_staff.employee e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name HAVING avg(e.salary) > 6000

question: Who reports to Bo, directly or through other managers?
expected_sql: WITH RECURSIVE reports AS (SELECT e.id, e.name FROM handmade_staff.employee e JOIN handmade_staff.employee b ON b.id = e.manager_id WHERE b.name = 'Bo' UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name FROM handmade_staff.employee e JOIN reports r ON e.manager_id = r.id) SELECT name FROM reports

question: On which days was a station warmer than on its previous reading day?
expected_sql: SELECT station, day FROM (SELECT s.name AS station, r.day, r.temperature, lag(r.temperature) OVER (PARTITION BY r.station_id ORDER BY r.day) AS previous_temperature FROM handmade_weather.reading r JOIN handmade_weather.station s ON s.id = r.station_id) days WHERE temperature > previous_temperature

question: Show each station's rainfall so far, day by day, ordered by station name and day.
expected_sql: SELECT s.name AS station, r.day, sum(r.rainfall_mm) OVER (PARTITION BY r.station_id ORDER BY r.day) AS rainfall_so_far FROM handmade_weather.reading r JOIN handmade_weather.station s ON s.id = r.station_id ORDER BY s.name, r.day

question: What share of each member's confirmation messages were confirmed, rounded to two decimals, with zero for members who got none?
expected_sql: SELECT m.name, round(coalesce(count(c.id) FILTER (WHERE c.action = 'confirmed')::numeric / nullif(count(c.id), 0), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate FROM handmade_signup.member m LEFT JOIN handmade_signup.confirmation c ON c.member_id = m.id GROUP BY m.id, m.name

question: List the names of everyone at the school, students and teachers alike.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM handmade_school.student UNION SELECT name FROM handmade_school.teacher

question: Which students take a course taught by Ms Wren?
expected_sql: SELECT s.name FROM handmade_school.student s WHERE s.id IN (SELECT e.student_id FROM handmade_school.enrollment e JOIN handmade_school.course c ON c.id = e.course_id JOIN handmade_school.teacher t ON t.id = c.teacher_id WHERE t.name = 'Ms Wren')
